question: A 33-year-old woman presents to a walk-in clinic for evaluation of some bumps around her eyes. The bumps are not itchy or painful. They have been getting larger since appearing last year. She has no other complaints. She has not sought out medical attention for the last 20 years due to lack of insurance coverage. Her medical history reveals no problems and she takes no medications. Her periods are regular. A review of systems reveals no other concerns. She does not drink, smoke, or use illicit drugs. Her vital signs show a heart rate of 86/min, respirations of 14/min, and blood pressure of 124/76 mm Hg. On examination, the rash is a series of small papules and plaques around her eyes. The rest of the examination is unremarkable. Which of the following initial blood tests are most appropriate at this time?

options.opb: Fasting blood glucose and lipid profile
options.ope: Fasting blood glucose, lipid profile, and thyroid stimulating hormone

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Bumps around eyes" -> "Non-itchy, non-painful" -> "Progressively enlarging" -> "Appeared last year" -> "No other complaints" -> "No medical attention for 20 years" -> "No medical problems in history" -> "No medications" -> "Regular periods" -> "No other concerns in review of systems" -> "Non-smoker, non-drinker, no illicit drug use" -> "Vital signs: HR 86/min, RR 14/min, BP 124/76 mm Hg" -> "Rash: small papules and plaques around eyes" -> "Rest of examination unremarkable" -> "Initial blood tests needed" -> 80%
analysis: Given the presentation of bumps around the eyes in a 33-year-old woman with no other complaints, a fasting blood glucose test alone may not be the most appropriate initial test. Considering the possibility of underlying conditions like dyslipidemia or thyroid dysfunction, it would be prudent to conduct a more comprehensive evaluation.
